entries.summary: The Damage Meter no longer counts as a gameplay mod online, and mod authors get the full list of run events.
highlights: Online: the Damage Meter is now treated as a client-only mod again, so running it no longer marks you as modded for public matchmaking.
Mod authors: 26 run events (hero death, chests, shop purchases, item and talent picks, chapter-end stats and more) are now listed with their fields in rsmm symbols events, and rsmm lint accepts them.
Mod authors: R.status.watch_stagger() and R.status.stagger() read stagger values, and the Lua API docs record which calls are proven in game.

entries.summary: Lua SDK: run-event catalog updated — 32 analytics events with their fields (hero_death, open_chest, sandman_buy, item/talent picks, chapter_end stats, ...); level_up_reach corrected to levelup_run
highlights: Lua SDK: run-event catalog updated — 32 analytics events with their fields (hero_death, open_chest, sandman_buy, item/talent picks, chapter_end stats, ...); level_up_reach corrected to levelup_run

entries.summary: Lua SDK: R.status.watch_stagger()/stagger() read the hero's stagger values; R.melody.choose documented as not working (melodies are random); R.revive, R.status.clear and R.run.lose marked proven
highlights: Lua SDK: R.status.watch_stagger()/stagger() read the hero's stagger values; R.melody.choose documented as not working (melodies are random); R.revive, R.status.clear and R.run.lose marked proven

entries.summary: Lua SDK: R.revive.tokens/add_token (experimental) — add party revive tokens during a run
highlights: Lua SDK: R.revive.tokens/add_token (experimental) — add party revive tokens during a run

entries.summary: New SDK APIs: R.melody.choose/remove by name (the old GUID-based choose never worked), R.control.lock/unlock/release, R.run.next_chapter/win/lose (current chapter only).
highlights: Mods can start collecting a melody by name, or remove one (R.melody.choose / remove)
Mods can freeze and release the player's controls (R.control.lock / release)
Mods can finish the chapter, win or lose the run (R.run.next_chapter / win / lose)

entries.summary: New SDK APIs: R.talent.reset / upgrade_random / upgrade_lowest / upgrade / add_random_ultimate change talents during a run; R.status.clear / clear_stagger cleanse the hero.
highlights: Mods can upgrade talents: random, lowest, a specific one, or straight to legendary (R.talent.upgrade*)
Mods can add a random ultimate talent or reset every talent (R.talent.add_random_ultimate / reset)
Mods can clear status effects and stagger (R.status.clear)

entries.summary: New SDK APIs: R.give.remove_random, R.give.remove_all and R.give.duplicate_random take items away or copy one, by rarity or for any.
highlights: Mods can remove a random item, or every item, of a rarity (R.give.remove_random / remove_all)
Mods can give a second copy of a random common, rare or epic item (R.give.duplicate_random)

entries.summary: New SDK APIs: R.ability (reset/reduce cooldowns, add/remove charges), R.shards.gain (shards as a pickup, gain bonuses apply), R.ingredient (add/remove keys and other ingredients), R.xp.set_level / set_xp.
highlights: Mods can reset or shorten ability cooldowns and add charges (R.ability)
Mods can give dream shards as a pickup, so shard-gain bonuses apply (R.shards.gain)
Mods can give or take keys and other ingredients (R.ingredient)
Mods can set the party level directly (R.xp.set_level)

entries.summary: Bug reports are easier to act on: the shared log now includes the health check and your loader version, and can be copied instead of uploaded.
highlights: Share log: the report now lists any problems the health check found and which loader you have installed, so whoever helps you sees the likely cause first.
Share log: "Copy report" puts the same redacted report on your clipboard if you would rather not upload it.
Mod authors: rsmm lint now catches Lua that reads a variable above the line that declares it (it is always nil in game), and POI components that would load but show no icon or prompt.
Mod authors: an item whose base is not a shipped item is now an error with a suggestion, instead of silently making nothing.

entries.summary: Fix: no online / no party code on Windows while the loader is installed (the 5.9.11 fix was incomplete)
highlights: Fix: no online / no party code on Windows while the loader is installed (the 5.9.11 fix was incomplete)

entries.summary: Online works again on Windows with RSMM, mods from the hub no longer stop the game from launching, and the Log screen can open and clear its logs.
highlights: Fixed: on Windows, launching through RSMM could leave you offline with no party code, even with no mods enabled. The game now uses Windows' own networking library while modded.
Fixed: "rsmm apply failed" (IndexError) on launch after installing No Overtime Tint, or another mod that edits game entities, from the hub.
Log screen: "Open folder" shows every saved run, and "Delete logs" clears them.
Shared logs and crash reports now show your real RSMM version instead of 0.0.0-dev.
Talent builder: "Hits apply a status" makes one of a hero's hits Chill, Ignite, Bleed, Weaken, make Vulnerable or Root while you own the talent (not yet tested in game).

entries.summary: Fix: online / party code failing on Windows while the loader is installed
highlights: Fix: online / party code failing on Windows while the loader is installed

entries.summary: Build your own talents in the editor: a new step-by-step builder, abilities that grow bigger, and effects borrowed from other heroes.
highlights: Editor: a new custom-talent builder. Pick the talent to replace, name it, and add building blocks or start from an example. Ideas it can't build yet ("POWER spawns a tornado") can be sent to us from the same screen.
Talent builder: "Make an ability bigger" grows an ability's area, length or width while you own the talent. Tested in game: Melusine's POWER area.
Talent builder: borrow a talent's effect from another hero (9 talents can move, e.g. Sun Wukong's Focused Strikes on Piper's Virtuoso). Its numbers follow your card's rarity.
Talent builder: bonuses that last until "your next ATTACK" and bonuses that can trigger "at most once every N seconds".
Editor: reopening a mod keeps your custom talents editable, and the editor says when it can't find the game.
For mod makers: rsmm diff shows what applying one mod changes, rsmm watch checks a mod before applying it, and mistyped mod names and commands get a suggestion.
Fixed: profile, install, sign-in and background-helper bugs in the app, and several security gaps.

entries.summary: Per-ability crit chance and cooldown reduction stats now read the right ability
highlights: Fixed: mods reading or changing one ability's crit chance or cooldown reduction got a different ability's stat

entries.summary: Mods can set each chapter's day/night timer
highlights: New: mods can change day/night length and boss timing per chapter (Chapter Timer)

entries.summary: Damage meter keeps each player's damage on their own row across chapters, plus stability fixes for mods
highlights: Damage meter: after a chapter change, a player's damage stays on their own row instead of moving to a new one
Damage meter: players who left the lobby no longer appear on the board
Damage meter: much less log spam during co-op runs
Mod settings: a mod that adjusts its own setting no longer freezes the game
Mods that read the camera, hero stats or XP no longer error between chapters
Fixed negative stat values showing as huge numbers

entries.summary: Mods that need your hero (like the camera mod) now work for everyone, and the Log starts empty until a game runs.
highlights: Fixed: the camera mod and other mods that read or change your hero did nothing unless a hidden loader setting had been switched on by hand. Settings > Loader features now has a Hero capture switch, and a mod that needs it switches it on for you when you apply.
Log: opens empty until a game is running, then shows that game live. Pick Last run or any earlier run in the list to read an old log.
For mod makers: `loader_flags = ["RSMM_ENABLE_HERO_CAPTURE"]` in [mod] asks for hero capture while your mod is enabled.

entries.summary: Talent builder: give one talent another talent's effect, and the Log no longer calls a finished game the current run.
highlights: Talent builder: "Also gives the effect of" on a card makes owning that talent also run another of the same hero's talents. Tested in game: Scarlet's Shapeshifter with Short Wick's bomb that explodes as soon as it lands.
Talent builder: the "... Count" stats are now labelled as tallies ("defensive objects held") and listed apart. They count things for other effects and do nothing on their own.
Fixed: the Log screen said "Current run" when no game was running. It now says "Last run", and notices a game started from Steam.

entries.summary: Mods you switch off in the Library now really stay off, and the talent builder learns "for a while after an ability".
highlights: Fixed: mods switched off in the Library were still installed when you launched the game. The Library is now what decides; mods in your profile folder that the Library shows as off are turned off before launch.
Talent builder: an added stat can now apply "For a while after" an ability, e.g. +25% damage for 3 seconds after POWER. Each use restarts the time.
Talent builder: stats are found by the words on the cards ("trait cooldown", "power charge"), and stats that would debuff your own hero (Ignite, Vulnerable, Rooted...) are greyed out.
Fixed: a talent with two added stats failed to build.
Editor: game-state values like "Is in cinematic" are no longer offered as stats, and "Reset everything" also clears test grants.

entries.summary: Fixes Launch on Linux, which started neither Steam nor the game.
highlights: Fixed (Linux): Launch did nothing. The app reported the game as started, but Steam and the game never opened. It now starts Steam properly, and if one way of reaching Steam fails it tries the next and tells you what went wrong.

entries.summary: Loader v27: logs why the game's WinHTTP calls fail (error code + which winhttp_real.dll is loaded) instead of claiming the backend redirect worked. Diagnostic for Windows players who see no party code on a self-hosted server.
highlights: Loader v27: logs why the game's WinHTTP calls fail (error code + which winhttp_real.dll is loaded) instead of claiming the backend redirect worked. Diagnostic for Windows players who see no party code on a self-hosted server.

entries.summary: Play on a community-hosted online server in one step, from Settings or with one command.
highlights: New: Settings > Game > Online server. Paste the address the host gave you and the app sets everything up, including installing or updating the loader when needed.
The same from the command line: `rsmm backend http://host:port` (and `rsmm backend off` to go back to the official servers). No more setx or Steam restarts.
Shows whether the server answers and whether your last game launch actually used it.
Fixed: `rsmm update-loader` said "up to date" when the game folder had no loader at all. It now says so.

entries.summary: Online backend redirect: set RSMM_BACKEND_URL=http://host:port to point the game at a self-hosted backend (services/stormancer). Off by default; with it unset the WinHTTP wrappers are a plain passthrough. Also adds a Steam web-ticket identity probe that logs the identity string and never the ticket.
highlights: Self-hosted online backend: point the game at your own server with RSMM_BACKEND_URL (off by default)
Steam web-ticket identity probe for backend setup (logs the identity, never the ticket)

entries.summary: Easier-to-read text throughout the app, and fewer background checks so screens open faster.
highlights: Easier to read: new fonts, upright labels instead of slanted ones, and larger small text. The fonts now ship inside the app, so it no longer contacts Google at launch and looks the same offline.
Fixed: file paths in Settings were shown in capital letters. They now show exactly as they are.
Fixed: the top bar no longer gets cut off at the default window size.
Faster: coming back to the Library no longer re-runs the update checks, and Settings reuses what the app already learned at launch.
Faster: the Profiles screen reads all your profiles in one step instead of one per profile.

entries.summary: A website refresh: easier-to-read fonts and a home page that leads with the registry. The app itself is unchanged.
highlights: Website: a redesigned home page that puts the download, a search box and the most popular mods first.
Website: easier-to-read fonts across every page, with the blackletter kept for the logo.
Website: removed the grey box that appeared on mod, guide and collection pages.
No changes to the app in this version.

entries.summary: Switching profiles no longer empties the one you left, every number on a talent card is editable, and cards link to the Ability editor.
highlights: Fixed: switching profiles no longer empties or mislabels the profile you left. Its mods stay put and are no longer shown as 'not on disk'.

Talent editor: every number a card shows can now be edited, including computed ones (like the Ice Clone's damage), single-number selectors and values with unusual names. Cards with nothing editable dropped from 144 to 22 of 460.
Talent editor: new 'Open in Ability editor' link on each card jumps to that talent's parts and links.
Publishing: the website's publish page fills in the mod id, name, version, tags and more from the manifest in your zip.

entries.summary: Block-based Scripts tab in the editor, faster talent cards, and editor tab fixes.
highlights: New: the editor's Scripts tab can build a script from blocks (Blockly) and writes the Lua for you.
Editor: faster talent cards, and a slow pick no longer lands on the wrong tab.
Fixed: clicking a pending-change chip no longer turns another tab into an item editor.
The loader's live config reload and R.camera arrive through the loader channel.

entries.summary: live config reload + R.camera
highlights: live config reload + R.camera

entries.summary: Custom heroes, one editor for items, talents, abilities and maps (also in your browser), much faster applies, and export of any of the game's models.
highlights: New for mod authors: custom heroes. A mod can add a hero of its own with its own name, body, weapons, outfits, numbers, abilities, attacks, talent cards and story pages.
New: one editor for items, talents, abilities and maps (rsmm editor), also at docs.rsmm.me/editor with nothing to install. Cards are drawn the way the game draws them.
The editor can open a mod you saved and keep working on it. Its new Scripts tab gives you items, talents and XP at the start of a run, so you can test a change at once.
Ability changes in the editor save straight into your custom hero.
Applying mods is much faster: a mod that did not change is not rebuilt, and an unchanged model or texture is not cooked again. A custom hero went from 46 seconds to under one.

New: rsmm export-model exports any of the game's 3001 models (scenery, props, enemies, NPCs) with textures and animations for Blender. export-character and import-character take a hero's body and animations out and back in.
More you can mod: animations, map chapters that generate from their own tiles, enemy copies, boss swaps, and the stat each item effect gives.
Fixed: an item copy marked unique_identity now really gets its own identity, so you can hold it and the original together.

entries.summary: Mods can give an item by its id (R.give.by_name), which the editor's test grants use. Fixed: a repeating main-thread task could run itself many times in one frame (a test grant handed out 66 items at once).
highlights: Mods can now hand you a specific item by its id; the editor's new test grants use this.
Fixed: a mod's repeating task could run many times in a single frame, so one test grant handed out dozens of items at once.

entries.summary: Run modifiers can now be read and changed by mods (No minimap proven in game); fixes reading global game values like the current chapter.
highlights: Run modifiers can now be read and changed by mods (No minimap proven in game); fixes reading global game values like the current chapter.

entries.summary: XP capture shared between mods; R.hero.entity() tells a custom hero from its base
highlights: XP capture shared between mods; R.hero.entity() tells a custom hero from its base

entries.summary: Removed R.mods.request (the abandoned in-game mod menu's intent queue). R.mods.list() is unchanged.
highlights: Removed R.mods.request (the abandoned in-game mod menu's intent queue). R.mods.list() is unchanged.

entries.summary: Stat modifiers now apply once instead of twice, show up on the in-run stat strip, and permanent ones last the whole run across chapters.
highlights: Stat modifiers now apply once instead of twice, show up on the in-run stat strip, and permanent ones last the whole run across chapters.

entries.summary: R.interact now reports the object you interacted with (ev.entity) and the hero doing it (ev.interactor); before, both pointed at the hero, so R.interact.name named your hero instead of the object.
highlights: R.interact now reports the object you interacted with (ev.entity) and the hero doing it (ev.interactor); before, both pointed at the hero, so R.interact.name named your hero instead of the object.

entries.summary: New R.hp reads and changes the hero's real health. R.shards replaces R.combat, which moved dream shards, not health; R.combat still works but logs a deprecation line. R.interact.name now names the object you interacted with.
highlights: New R.hp reads and changes the hero's real health. R.shards replaces R.combat, which moved dream shards, not health; R.combat still works but logs a deprecation line. R.interact.name now names the object you interacted with.

entries.summary: Mod load problems now show up as errors: a broken init.lua, a manifest that fails to parse, or a mod skipped after a crash appear in rsmm log --errors and the desktop problems filter.
highlights: Mod load problems now show up as errors: a broken init.lua, a manifest that fails to parse, or a mod skipped after a crash appear in rsmm log --errors and the desktop problems filter.

entries.summary: Mods can now tell which object an interaction happened on, so a mod-made point of interest can respond when you use it.
highlights: New for mod authors: an interaction event now reports WHICH object it fired on, so a mod can react to its own point of interest instead of to every chest and fountain in the run.
The object is carried through to the success step, which is the one mods actually act on — before, only the initial request knew what had been used.
Custom points of interest are no longer experimental: a mod-made structure generates on the map, draws its own minimap icon, and can be interacted with.
Removed a debug trace that aimed at an address the current game build no longer has, so it could never do anything but disable itself.

entries.summary: Talent mods can now add new behaviour to a hero, not just change numbers, and you can publish mods to the store straight from the command line.
highlights: New for mod authors: a talent mod can copy parts of a hero's talent logic and rewire them, so a talent can gain a new effect. For example, the attack after a dash can become the combo finisher, or a talent can summon rats every few attacks.
New for mod authors: a talent mod can borrow an effect another hero already has, such as Beowulf's TRAIT cooldown reduction, and give it to a different hero's talent.
Talent cards written by mods show real numbers that grow with rarity, like the game's own cards, instead of placeholder values.
Several talent or text changes in one mod now all apply. Before, only the last one took effect.
Relabelling Sun Wukong's talents works; his text could not be found before.
New CLI command: rsmm publish uploads a mod to the store, signed in with a personal API token.

entries.summary: Edit the Sandman's shop from a config screen dressed in the game's own art, a new item-grid config editor for mod authors, and a local 3D map-generation editor.
highlights: New for mod authors: the shop content kind edits the Sandman's shop. Set prices, choose which items each offer slot sells (including Grimoire, Astral and Wishing Well powerups), and replace the random magical-object offers with items you pick.

New for mod authors: the item-grid config field. A mod declares sections, filters, counts, a per-item number and an optional theme of game textures in config_schema.toml, and the app draws the editor. Textures are read from your own install, never shipped with a mod.
Config dialogs for grid editors open wide and lay their sections out side by side, sized to the window and your UI scale.
A shop edit that would crash the game when the Sandman's shop opens (a Minor row with fewer than two items) is refused before it is applied.
New CLI command: rsmm map-editor opens a local 3D editor for a chapter's tile-generation recipe.
Applying mods cleans up files from content you removed, and merged text banks land in the right mods folder.

entries.summary: Faster hero detection, runtime entity spawning for mods, in-run talent grants, run-state reads, and a much quieter loader log.
highlights: Mods that use your hero (stats, talents, damage meter) start working within a second of a run starting. Before, they could wait up to two minutes, until your first dream-shard pickup.
New for mod authors: R.spawn creates a copy of an entity in the world, such as another enemy beside the hero.
New for mod authors: R.talent.grant gives the hero a talent mid-run, so a modded talent can be tested without waiting for the game to offer it.
New for mod authors: R.game reads the run's own state, such as the current chapter, whether you are in the shop, and whether you are the session host.
The loader log is far shorter. Debug traces no longer flag every level as an error, and rsmm doctor warns when a debug trace flag is left switched on.

entries.summary: Five reported bugs: the store-page arrow in the list view, Open folder doing nothing, a duplicated profile losing every mod, scrolling that dropped you back where you came from, and collections landing in a profile named after nothing.
highlights: The arrow beside a mod in list view opens its store page again. In list view it was wired to nothing at all.

Open folder in Profiles works. In the AppImage it was launching the file manager with the app's own bundled GTK libraries, which killed it on startup — silently, because nothing was waiting to hear about it.

Duplicating a profile keeps its mods. The copy took the profile's list but not its files, and since the app reads mods from whichever profile is active, the copy AND the original looked empty until you switched back.
Scrolling stays where you put it. If anything else moved the page mid-scroll — a scrollbar drag, a list growing — the wheel animation kept chasing its old destination and dragged you back to it.
Installing a collection with no profile selected creates one named after the collection, instead of a generic “My Mods”.

entries.summary: A visual overhaul of the whole app: readable text, one consistent shape language, and cards that line up. Plus a fix for the stale strips of the previous page that appeared while scrolling.
highlights: The app has been redrawn. Panels and cards now sit on their own surfaces instead of each carrying a border, so the screen has a foreground and a background again.
Body text is legible. The greys it was set in fell below the accessible contrast floor, and error messages were the worst offender of all.
Scrolling no longer leaves fragments of the previous page behind.
Mod cards in the Library are the same height, with the description clipped to three lines, so a long summary stops knocking the grid out of line.
The enable switch is a real toggle, and Uninstall is quiet until you reach for it — it used to be the boldest thing on every card.
Filters read as a list of choices rather than a heap of buttons, and labels are in sentence case instead of tracked-out capitals.
Corners, focus rings and button styles are consistent across every screen.
The 'Ready to restart' dialog after a Linux AppImage update is legible: its notice used to render as a wall of capitals.

entries.summary: Overlay HUDs stop launching a background process every second while you play, the window remembers where you left it, uninstalling asks first, and toolbars no longer run off the edge in a smaller window.
highlights: Overlay HUDs no longer start a background process once a second while the game is running — they read the mod's data straight from disk instead.
The window remembers its size and position between launches, and refuses to reopen off-screen if you unplug the monitor it was on.
Uninstalling a mod asks first. Uninstalling several reports each one, so a single failure no longer silently abandons the rest.
Buttons, cards and toolbars no longer overflow when the window is not full width — the Profiles actions and the Browse install button especially.
A mod versioned 1.0 is no longer treated as older than 1.0.0, which left an update badge showing forever and reinstalled the mod on every 'Update all'.
The Conflicts screen no longer reports 'all quiet' while it is still checking, or after the check fails.
Dialogs close with Escape and move focus into themselves, so they can be answered without tabbing through the whole app first.
Load order can be rearranged from the keyboard with Alt+Up / Alt+Down.
Settings no longer rewrites its whole store on every keystroke while you type a path.
Commands that rewrite the game install — Apply, Restore, Build, Doctor + repair — now confirm before running.

entries.summary: Loader/SDK v12: hero-select unlock progression, duplicate-hero availability gate, cross-chapter enemy mixing, stale value-context crash fix, guarded Entity_ModifyHealth walks, resource-resolve tracing.
highlights: Loader/SDK v12: hero-select unlock progression, duplicate-hero availability gate, cross-chapter enemy mixing, stale value-context crash fix, guarded Entity_ModifyHealth walks, resource-resolve tracing.

entries.summary: Pick the monsters each chapter spawns. An enemy mod's chapters are now editable from its Config panel — a searchable list of every creature in the game, grouped by the chapter it ships in, so you can put Storm Island crabs in the Dark Hills or turn one chapter into a single monster. Picks apply on a plain install: the cooked definitions are read straight out of the game folder, so no 7 GB asset dump is needed any more. Also fixes the download count breaking across two lines on a mod card.
highlights: Enemy mods get a per-chapter monster picker: add, remove, or move a creature to another chapter.
Picking now works on a normal install, not just a developer checkout.
Mod cards no longer wrap the download count into the star rating.
New: rsmm assets search <text> finds a cooked asset by its readable path.

entries.summary: Cross-chapter enemy randomisation works. A mod can now draw every biome's monsters from the whole game — chapter 1 spawning crabs, gargoyles and cultists alongside its own — without the chapter-2 crash or black screen that made the feature unusable. The cause was the step that rewrote each biome's spawn pool, and it turned out to be unnecessary: an imported creature is already preloaded by the definition that points at it. Enemy mods add repoint_pools = false to use it.
highlights: Enemy mods can mix monsters across every chapter without crashing on a chapter transition.
The unlock and hero-select work in this build is inert unless a mod asks for it.

entries.summary: Fixes the loader log being unreadable on a non-English Windows. The log is written as UTF-8, but the app read it with whatever encoding the system locale preferred — so on a Chinese, Russian or Japanese Windows every dash and every non-ASCII player name came out as mojibake, in the Log screen and in any log shared for support.
highlights: Loader log reads correctly on every system locale — player names with non-Latin characters are no longer mangled.
Shared diagnostic logs can now be opened by an assistant the user sends the link to, instead of only by a human.

entries.summary: Loader log: the boot line that counted the IO-hook override table said 'active overrides=N'. That table is only read by the IO hook (off unless RSMM_ENABLE_IO=1) and counts files under mods/*/assets, which apply never populates — so a fully-applied install always read 'active overrides=0', which looks like none of your mods are working. The line now names itself and points at rsmm doctor.
highlights: Loader log no longer reports "active overrides=0" on a healthy install — that line counted a subsystem that is off by default and never meant what it looked like.
